chapter: Young Excelsior and the old-time band scene
title: Interview opening; reviving the Young Excelsior band
summary: Russell and Collins open the session. Robertson explains that he and others renewed the Excelsior name after the old members died out, with only three originals left.

story.theme_name: Starting the tape: names, dates and places
story.community_name: Interview openings: names, dates and tape setup

blocks.x: The date is September the 23rd, I believe, 22nd or 23rd, anyway, 1961. There's the calendar over that. And this is Bill Russell and Ralph Collins, interviewing Mr. Robertson. Do you mind giving your full name, Mr. Robertson? Henry Robertson. Henry, any middle name?
You were saying about this, the young Excelsior.

Yeah, the young Excelsior. You see, they had the old Excelsior. Well, so many of the old fellas died out. Well, then lots of them come and say, you know, they'd kill about picking. It'd take like me and several more others who wasn't going to let it go down. We just picked it up and picked up the best men that we knew that could compare with the men that had dropped out. We just renewed the name and went on out again.
Do you have any members in this young Excelsior band that were also in the old Excelsior band?

Me? The fellow played Triney. He played with them. And I think they had three or four was in there. But we were only three. Only three left. The others all practically died out. That's Ewan Wilson and Wilson. And this boy played, Buster played with him several times. But he wasn't, he was young, young, young, young, young, but you couldn't even, you know, count him. Because you couldn't even put him in there. But we got him playing plus nine. But he's just about as good as them as playing the old Excelsior at that time. Yeah, he's good. Yeah, he's very good. Yeah, he's good. We got some fellas from New York down here now. Wants to take us over, some white fellas. But Buster went up there and they took a light on the bus and didn't have any plenty. Him and his sons down here now.
Oh yeah, Crank Bay. Yeah. Crank, something like that.
